name.text: Finding the Area of a Regular Pentagon

questiontext.text:
Find the area of the figure below, centered at \(O\).

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="300px"]] var b = {#base_length#}; var s = {#slant#}; // Abstract geometric scaling for a clean visual representation var R = 20; var angle = Math.PI / 5; // 36 degrees // Generous bounding box to prevent clipping the top vertex or base label // 500x300 canvas ratio requires a wider X span to keep Aspect Ratio true var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, { boundingbox: [-40, 25, 40, -25], maxboundingbox: [-60, 40, 60, -40], axis: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false }); // Pentagon Vertices var p0 = board.create('point', [0, R], {visible: false}); var p1 = board.create('point', [-R * Math.sin(2*angle), R * Math.cos(2*angle)], {visible: false}); var p2 = board.create('point', [-R * Math.sin(angle), -R * Math.cos(angle)], {visible: false}); var p3 = board.create('point', [R * Math.sin(angle), -R * Math.cos(angle)], {visible: false}); var p4 = board.create('point', [R * Math.sin(2*angle), R * Math.cos(2*angle)], {visible: false}); var center = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: 'O', visible: true, label:{offset:[-5,15]}}); board.create('polygon', [p0, p1, p2, p3, p4], { fillColor: '#fafafa', strokeColor: '#212121', strokeWidth: 2 }); // Slanted lines (radii) board.create('segment', [center, p3], {strokeColor: '#1976d2'}); board.create('segment', [center, p2], {strokeColor: '#1976d2'}); // Perpendicular height (apothem) var mid = board.create('midpoint', [p2, p3], {visible: false}); board.create('segment', [center, mid], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#d32f2f'}); // Right angle marker var rad = R * 0.15; board.create('angle', [p3, mid, center], {type: 'square', radius: rad, strokeColor: '#d32f2f', name: ''}); // Dynamic Labels securely anchored board.create('text', [0, -R * Math.cos(angle) - 2.5, b + " cm"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 14}); board.create('text', [R * Math.sin(angle)/2 + 2, -R * Math.cos(angle)/2, s + " cm"], {anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 14, strokeColor: '#1976d2'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

\(\text{Area} =\) [[input:ans1]] \(\text{cm}^2\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

To calculate the area of the pentagon, divide the shape into five identical isosceles triangles by joining each vertex to the centre \(O\).

Each triangle has:

  • base length \(= {@base_length@}\text{ cm}\)
  • two equal slanted sides of \(= {@slant@}\text{ cm}\)

To find the perpendicular height (\(h\)) of one triangle, we split it into two right-angled triangles. The hypotenuse is the slanted side, and the base of this smaller triangle is exactly half of the total base:

\[ \text{Half base} = \frac{{@base_length@}}{2} = {@half_base@}\text{ cm} \]

Using Pythagoras’ theorem (\(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\)):

\[ \begin{aligned} h^2 + ({@half_base@})^2 &= ({@slant@})^2 \\ h^2 &= {@slant^2@} - {@half_base^2@} \\ h &= \sqrt{{@slant^2 - half_base^2@}} \\ h &= {@height@}\text{ cm} \end{aligned} \]

The area of one full isosceles triangle is therefore:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area of one triangle} &= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times h \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \times {@base_length@} \times {@height@} \\ &= {@area_triangle@}\text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned} \]

Since the pentagon consists of five identical triangles, its total area is:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Total Area} &= 5 \times {@area_triangle@} \\ \text{Total Area} &= {@ta@}\text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned} \]
